events.title: John Baptizes in the Wilderness
events.description: John appears in the Judean wilderness calling people to repentance and baptizing them in the Jordan. He announces that a more powerful successor will baptize with the Holy Spirit.

events.title: John Baptizes Jesus
events.description: Jesus comes from Nazareth and is baptized by John. As he emerges from the water, the Spirit descends upon him and a heavenly voice identifies him as the beloved Son.

events.title: Jesus Is Tested in the Wilderness
events.description: The Spirit drives Jesus into the wilderness for forty days, where Satan tests him among the wild animals and angels attend him.

events.title: Jesus Begins Proclaiming in Galilee
events.description: After John is arrested, Jesus enters Galilee announcing the nearness of God's kingdom and calling for repentance and trust in the good news.

events.title: Jesus Calls Four Fishermen
events.description: Beside the Sea of Galilee, Jesus calls Simon and Andrew, then James and John, away from their fishing work. All four leave their nets and families to follow him.

events.title: Jesus Teaches and Exorcises at Capernaum
events.description: Jesus teaches in the Capernaum synagogue with striking authority and commands an unclean spirit to leave a man. News of the encounter spreads throughout Galilee.

events.title: Jesus Heals at Simon's House
events.description: Jesus raises Simon's feverish mother-in-law, who resumes serving the household. After sunset the town gathers at the door, and Jesus heals many sick people and casts out demons.

events.title: Jesus Tours Galilee
events.description: After praying alone, Jesus travels through Galilee preaching in synagogues and expelling demons. He cleanses a man with a skin disease, whose widespread report makes public entry into towns difficult.

events.title: A Paralytic Is Forgiven and Healed
events.description: Four people lower a paralyzed man through the roof of a crowded Capernaum house. Jesus first declares his sins forgiven and then heals him, answering scribes who question his authority.

events.title: Jesus Calls Levi and Eats with Outcasts
events.description: Jesus calls Levi from the tax booth and later shares a meal with many tax collectors and sinners. He answers critics by describing his mission as a summons to those who need restoration.

events.title: Jesus Is Questioned about Fasting
events.description: Asked why his disciples do not fast, Jesus compares his presence to a wedding celebration and anticipates a future absence. Images of unshrunk cloth and new wine emphasize the incompatibility of old forms and the new moment.

events.title: The Disciples Pluck Grain on the Sabbath
events.description: Pharisees challenge the disciples for plucking grain on the Sabbath. Jesus appeals to David's need and teaches that the Sabbath serves humanity under the authority of the Son of Man.

events.title: Jesus Heals a Withered Hand
events.description: In a synagogue Jesus restores a man's withered hand after confronting observers about doing good on the Sabbath. Pharisees and Herodians then begin plotting against him.

events.title: Crowds Gather beside the Sea
events.description: Large crowds from Galilee and surrounding regions press toward Jesus because of his healings. He cures many and silences unclean spirits that recognize him.

events.title: Jesus Appoints the Twelve
events.description: On a mountain Jesus selects twelve companions to remain with him and to be sent out to preach with authority over demons. Mark names the group, including Judas Iscariot.

events.title: Jesus Answers Charges about His Power
events.description: Jesus' family seeks to restrain him while Jerusalem scribes attribute his exorcisms to the ruler of demons. Jesus exposes the charge as self-defeating and identifies those who do God's will as his true family.

events.title: Jesus Teaches in Parables by the Sea
events.description: From a boat Jesus teaches a large crowd through parables of soils, a lamp, secretly growing seed, and a mustard seed. He later explains the purpose of parables and the sower's meaning to his disciples.

events.title: Jesus Calms a Storm
events.description: A violent windstorm threatens the disciples' boat while Jesus sleeps. He stills the wind and sea, then challenges their fear and lack of faith.

events.title: Jesus Frees the Gerasene Man
events.description: In Gentile territory Jesus expels a multitude of demons from a man living among tombs; the spirits enter pigs that rush into the sea. The restored man is sent home to report God's mercy throughout the Decapolis.

events.title: A Woman Is Healed and Jairus's Daughter Raised
events.description: While Jesus goes to help Jairus's dying daughter, a woman suffering twelve years touches his clothing and is healed. Despite news of the girl's death, Jesus enters her room and restores her to life.

events.title: Nazareth Rejects Jesus
events.description: People in Jesus' hometown take offense at the familiar craftsman and his family despite his synagogue teaching. Their unbelief limits his works there, though he heals a few sick people.

events.title: The Twelve Are Sent in Pairs
events.description: Jesus sends the twelve out two by two with authority over unclean spirits and instructions to travel lightly. They preach repentance, expel demons, and heal the sick.

events.title: Herod Executes John the Baptist
events.description: Herod recalls imprisoning John for condemning his marriage to Herodias. Bound by a banquet oath after Herodias's daughter dances, he orders John beheaded and the disciples bury the body.

events.title: Jesus Feeds Five Thousand
events.description: The returning apostles withdraw with Jesus, but a large crowd reaches the deserted place first. Jesus teaches them and multiplies five loaves and two fish so that all eat and twelve baskets remain.

events.title: Jesus Walks across the Sea
events.description: After praying alone, Jesus approaches the disciples' struggling boat by walking on the water and the wind ceases when he joins them. At Gennesaret, people bring the sick from across the region and those who touch his cloak are healed.

events.title: Jesus Challenges Traditions about Defilement
events.description: Pharisees and scribes criticize the disciples' unwashed hands. Jesus condemns traditions that displace God's commands and teaches that harmful intentions arising from within, rather than food entering the body, defile a person.

events.title: A Gentile Woman's Daughter Is Freed
events.description: In the region of Tyre, a Syrophoenician woman persistently asks Jesus to expel a demon from her daughter. Jesus grants her request, and she finds the child restored at home.

events.title: Jesus Heals a Deaf Man
events.description: In the Decapolis people bring Jesus a man who cannot hear and speaks with difficulty. Jesus privately restores his hearing and speech, and the astonished crowd spreads the news despite being told not to.

events.title: Jesus Feeds Four Thousand
events.description: Jesus has compassion on a crowd that has remained with him for three days without food. Seven loaves and a few fish feed four thousand people, with seven baskets left over.

events.title: Jesus Refuses a Sign and Warns the Disciples
events.description: Jesus refuses the Pharisees' demand for a heavenly sign. In the boat he warns against the influence of the Pharisees and Herod, while the disciples misunderstand him as speaking about their lack of bread.

events.title: A Blind Man at Bethsaida Is Healed in Stages
events.description: Jesus leads a blind man outside Bethsaida and restores his sight through two acts of healing. Once the man sees clearly, Jesus sends him directly home.

events.title: Peter Identifies Jesus as Messiah
events.description: Near Caesarea Philippi, the disciples report public opinions about Jesus. Peter identifies him as the Messiah, and Jesus orders them not to publicize the conclusion.

events.title: Jesus Foretells His Death and Defines Discipleship
events.description: Jesus teaches that he will be rejected, killed, and rise after three days. He rebukes Peter's resistance and summons the crowd to costly, self-denying discipleship.

events.title: Jesus Is Transfigured
events.description: Six days later Jesus takes Peter, James, and John up a mountain, where his appearance changes and Elijah and Moses appear. A cloud identifies him as the beloved Son, and afterward he discusses Elijah's coming with the disciples.

events.title: Jesus Frees a Boy from a Spirit
events.description: Jesus returns to find the disciples unable to expel a destructive spirit from a boy. He responds to the father's struggling faith, commands the spirit to leave, and later teaches the disciples about prayer.

events.title: Jesus Again Foretells His Death
events.description: While traveling quietly through Galilee, Jesus again predicts his betrayal, death, and resurrection. In Capernaum he counters the disciples' argument about greatness by placing a child among them and teaching humble service.

events.title: Jesus Teaches about Allies and Stumbling
events.description: Jesus tells the disciples not to stop an outsider who uses his name to expel demons. He warns strongly against causing vulnerable believers or oneself to stumble and urges the group to live at peace.

events.title: Jesus Teaches in Judea about Marriage and Children
events.description: In Judea Jesus answers a test about divorce by appealing to God's purpose in creation and later explains the matter privately. He welcomes children whom the disciples try to turn away and presents them as models for receiving God's kingdom.

events.title: A Wealthy Man Turns Away
events.description: A man seeking eternal life tells Jesus he has kept the commandments, but grieves when asked to relinquish his wealth and follow. Jesus teaches the disciples about wealth's danger and God's ability to accomplish what humans cannot.

events.title: Jesus Foretells His Death a Third Time
events.description: On the road toward Jerusalem, Jesus privately gives the twelve a detailed prediction of his condemnation, abuse, execution by Gentiles, and resurrection after three days.

events.title: James and John Seek Places of Honor
events.description: James and John ask for prominent positions in Jesus' glory, angering the other disciples. Jesus contrasts domineering rulers with a community in which greatness consists in service and his own life is given for many.

events.title: Jesus Heals Bartimaeus
events.description: As Jesus leaves Jericho, the blind beggar Bartimaeus repeatedly appeals to him as David's son. Jesus credits his faith, restores his sight, and Bartimaeus follows on the road.

events.title: Jesus Enters Jerusalem
events.description: Jesus approaches Jerusalem on a colt while crowds spread cloaks and branches and acclaim the coming Davidic kingdom. He surveys the temple and returns to Bethany with the twelve.

events.title: Jesus Drives Commerce from the Temple
events.description: Jesus condemns a fruitless fig tree and then disrupts buying, selling, and money changing in the temple, teaching that the sanctuary should serve all nations in prayer. The withered tree later becomes an occasion to teach about faith, prayer, and forgiveness.

events.title: Jerusalem Leaders Challenge Jesus' Authority
events.description: Chief priests, scribes, and elders demand the source of Jesus' authority. He answers with a question about John's baptism that they decline to resolve for fear of the crowd.

events.title: Jesus Tells the Parable of the Violent Tenants
events.description: Jesus describes tenants who abuse a landowner's servants and kill his beloved son before losing the vineyard. The leaders recognize the parable as directed against them but withdraw because they fear the crowd.

events.title: Jesus Answers Questions about Tax and Resurrection
events.description: Jesus avoids a trap about imperial tax by distinguishing what belongs to the emperor from what belongs to God. He then answers Sadducees by teaching that resurrection life differs from marriage and that God is God of the living.

events.title: Jesus Names the Greatest Commandments
events.description: A scribe asks which commandment is foremost. Jesus joins wholehearted love of God with love of one's neighbor, and the scribe agrees that these surpass sacrifices.

events.title: Jesus Teaches about David, Scribes, and a Widow
events.description: Jesus questions how the Messiah can be merely David's son, warns against status-seeking scribes who exploit widows, and points to a poor widow whose two small coins constitute her whole livelihood.

events.title: Jesus Foretells the Temple's Fall
events.description: On the Mount of Olives Jesus predicts the temple's destruction and warns his disciples of deception, conflict, persecution, and severe distress. He promises the gathering of the elect and repeatedly urges vigilance because the final hour is unknown.

events.title: A Woman Anoints Jesus at Bethany
events.description: Two days before Passover, leaders seek a discreet way to kill Jesus. At Simon's house a woman pours costly perfume on Jesus, which he interprets as preparation for burial; Judas then arranges to betray him.

events.title: Jesus Shares the Passover Meal
events.description: The disciples prepare Passover in an upper room, where Jesus identifies an impending betrayal. He distributes bread and a cup as signs of his body and covenant blood and anticipates sharing wine anew in God's kingdom.

events.title: Jesus Prays in Gethsemane
events.description: After predicting that the disciples will desert him and Peter will deny him, Jesus prays in deep anguish at Gethsemane. Three times his closest disciples fall asleep while he submits to the Father's will.

events.title: Judas Betrays and Jesus Is Arrested
events.description: Judas identifies Jesus with a kiss to an armed group sent by Jerusalem authorities. Jesus is seized, one bystander wounds the high priest's servant, and all the disciples flee.

events.title: The Council Condemns Jesus as Peter Denies Him
events.description: The council struggles to establish consistent testimony before condemning Jesus after the high priest questions him about his identity. In the courtyard Peter denies knowing Jesus three times and weeps when the rooster confirms the prediction.

events.title: Pilate Hands Jesus Over for Crucifixion
events.description: Jerusalem's leaders deliver Jesus to Pilate and accuse him as king of the Jews. Pilate releases Barabbas at the crowd's demand, has Jesus flogged, and turns him over to soldiers who mock and abuse him.

events.title: Jesus Is Crucified and Dies
events.description: Simon of Cyrene is compelled to carry the cross before Jesus is crucified at Golgotha between two bandits. Darkness covers the land, Jesus dies, the temple curtain tears, and a centurion identifies him as God's Son while women followers watch.

events.title: Joseph of Arimathea Buries Jesus
events.description: Before the Sabbath, Joseph of Arimathea obtains Jesus' body from Pilate, wraps it in linen, and places it in a rock-cut tomb sealed with a stone. Mary Magdalene and Mary mother of Joses observe the burial place.

events.title: Women Find the Tomb Empty
events.description: After the Sabbath, Mary Magdalene, Mary mother of James, and Salome find the tomb open and Jesus' body absent. A young man announces that Jesus has risen and directs them toward Galilee, but they flee in fear and amazement.

events.title: The Longer Ending Recounts Appearances and Commission
events.description: The longer textual ending reports appearances to Mary Magdalene, two travelers, and the eleven, followed by a worldwide commission. It concludes with Jesus' ascension and the disciples' preaching accompanied by signs.
